single_sided: rho- = pi- = 0  =>  pi_eff/rho_eff = pi+/rho+ : k+, k- and Delta k drop out exactly
same_closure: pi+- = c rho+-  =>  pi_eff/rho_eff = c : k's drop out exactly
general: pi+- = (cbar +- dc/2) rho+-  =>  pi_eff/rho_eff = cbar + (dc/2) A,  A = (k- rho+ + k+ rho-)/(k- rho+ - k+ rho-)
reading: Amplification needs BOTH dark radiation on both sides that nearly cancels in k- rho+ - k+ rho- AND different closures on the two sides (dc != 0). Delta k does not appear on its own. The earlier statements 'near-symmetric bubble amplifies by k/(k- - k+)' (P0 O2, Phase 2 J1) were too strong and are corrected.
status_change: Delta k leaves the open list: for single-sided feeding it is irrelevant to the closure; for two-sided feeding what matters is the split k- rho+ vs k+ rho-, which is part of the flux-source specification.
